title: When are the two moving points closest, and when farthest?
description: A point X moves along one side of a rectangle and a point Y moves along the opposite side. The length XY is seven centimetres when the points are level, and about eight centimetres one millimetre when they sit at opposite corners. Keeko's doubt is that a slanting line is shorter than a straight one.
teaching_notes: One idea: XY is shortest when X and Y are level, and longest when they sit at opposite corners, because a slant covers the gap across and also the gap up. Watch for students who think a slanting line is shorter than a straight one.

source: In rectangle ABCD with AB = 7 cm and BC = 4 cm, X moves alon
video_script.why: A learner finds the positions of two moving points on opposite sides of a rectangle that make the joining length shortest and longest.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle with one side seven centimetres and the next side four centimetres, and its two moving points
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with a point X sliding on one side and a point Y sliding on the opposite side
video_script.wrong_answer: a slanting line is shorter than a straight one
video_script.wrong_move: believes the slanting line XY is shorter than the level line XY because it looks tilted and tucked in
video_script.payoff_line: Ex why is shortest when level and longest corner to corner.

final_answer.value: Closest: X and Y level, XY = 7 cm. Farthest: opposite corners, XY about 8 cm 1 mm

maths_rules: X and Y at the same distance from A and B: XY runs level with AB, so XY = AB = 7 cm
X and Y not level: XY slants and is longer than 7 cm
X at A and Y at C (or X at D and Y at B): XY is the diagonal AC
AC = square root of (7 times 7 plus 4 times 4) = square root of 65, about 8.06 cm, about 8 cm 1 mm
video_script.design: Two moving points are shown level, then slanted, then at opposite corners, with the length XY compared each time.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The point ex moves along one side, and the point why moves along the opposite side.
When do you think they are closest, and when farthest?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: rectangle ABCD with X on AD and Y on BC

marks.rect: the rectangle ABCD is labelled with its sides
marks.move: X slides along AD and Y slides along BC

narration: <bookmark mark='rect'/>Take the rectangle eigh bee cee dee, with eigh bee seven centimetres and bee cee four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='move'/>Ex slides along eigh dee, and why slides along bee cee.
Each pair of positions gives a new length ex why.

beats.on_screen: Given: rectangle ABCD, AB = 7 cm, BC = 4 cm; X on AD, Y on BC
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rectangle with ex on eigh dee and why on bee cee.

beats.on_screen: To find: where XY is shortest and where it is longest

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find where ex why is shortest and where it is longest.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: X and Y at equal distances from A and B; XY runs level with AB and XY = 7 cm

marks.level: X and Y are placed at the same height
marks.flat: XY is drawn level and measured as 7 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='level'/>Step one, place ex and why at the same distance from eigh and bee.
<bookmark mark='flat'/>Then ex why runs level with eigh bee, and it measures seven centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: slide X up and Y down; XY slants and is longer than 7 cm

marks.slant: X slides up and Y slides down
marks.longer: the slanting XY is measured as more than 7 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='slant'/>Step two, slide ex up the side and why down the side.
<bookmark mark='longer'/>Ex why now slants across, and it measures more than seven centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: X at A and Y at C, opposite corners; XY is the diagonal AC, about 8 cm 1 mm

marks.far: X moves to A and Y moves to C
marks.diag: XY becomes the diagonal AC and is measured

narration: <bookmark mark='far'/>Step three, place ex at eigh and why at cee, the opposite corners.
<bookmark mark='diag'/>Ex why is now the diagonal eigh cee, and it measures about eight centimetres one millimetre.

beats.on_screen: Answer: closest when level, XY = 7 cm; farthest at opposite corners, XY about 8 cm 1 mm

marks.res: the level and the corner positions glow

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ex why is shortest when level and longest corner to corner.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Level, it is seven centimetres. At opposite corners, it is about eight centimetres one millimetre.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the level XY and the slanting XY drawn together; the slanting one is traced as across and also up, and it is longer

marks.doubt: the slanting line and the level line appear together
marks.fix: the slanting line is traced as a step across and a step up
marks.keep: the slanting line is laid beside the level one and is seen to be longer

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a slanting line is shorter than a straight one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a slanting ex why goes across, and it also goes up.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>It covers more ground than the straight line, so the level position is the shortest.
